verdict.summary_for_david: I am stopping this loop. PR #90 adds the D2 merge-opinion role — the thing that tells you, independently of Claude's own account, what a pull request actually is and what it does not do. Three review rounds found 7, then 4, then 2 problems, every one of them inside the code this PR changed, and the first eleven were fixed: the role was wired into the close-out sequence so it cannot ship dormant, it stopped inventing an "approve the merge" line when it had no recommendation to give, it stopped mangling quoted text into run-on prose, and it stopped presenting a closed review thread as proof a defect was actually fixed. The two left over are both about the wording and bookkeeping of a document that decides nothing — it is written for you to read, and no gate, receipt or automatic step consumes it. One is a stale sentence in the role's instructions that the document it actually receives now contradicts in plain terms; the other is a missing sanity check that would matter only if the command were run in the wrong repository, where the brief would carry a title and commit you would not recognise. Neither can delete anything, corrupt the machinery that tracks reviews, or give the agents more authority than they have, which is the bar internal tooling has to clear before it is worth another round — so I am recording both as known gaps rather than buying a fourth round to polish them. Two things worth knowing: nothing has changed on the branch since the round-3 review, so what merges is exactly what was reviewed; and this PR was declared "trivial" for provenance purposes despite being a thousand new lines across ten files, which meant I had no approved statement of intent to judge any of the thirteen findings against. That did not change my answer here, but it is the kind of declaration worth getting right, since it quietly removes one of the tools I use to tell a real defect from work that was never in scope.
